scheme_name: Horticulture Development Programme for NE and Himalayan States
overview: The Horticulture Development Programme for NE and Himalayan States is a sub-scheme of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), implemented by State Horticulture Missions (SHM) in the North Eastern States and Himalayan States. It aims to promote holistic growth of the horticulture sector, including bamboo and coconut, through regionally differentiated strategies covering research, technology promotion, extension, post-harvest management, processing, and marketing. The scheme encourages farmer aggregation into groups like FIGs/FPOs/FPCs to achieve economies of scale, enhances production and farmers' income, strengthens nutritional security, improves productivity via quality germplasm and micro-irrigation, and supports skill development and employment generation for rural youth in horticulture and post-harvest management, especially in the cold chain sector.
geographic_scope: North Eastern States and Himalayan States
objectives: Promote holistic growth of horticulture sector, including bamboo and coconut through area based regionally differentiated strategies
Encourage aggregation of farmers into farmer groups like FIGs/FPOs and FPCs to bring economy of scale and scope
Enhance horticulture production, augment farmers, income and strengthen nutritional security
Improve productivity by way of quality germplasm, planting material and water use efficiency through Micro Irrigation
Support skill development and create employment generation opportunities for rural youth in horticulture and post harvest management, especially in the cold chain sector
eligibility: Farmers / beneficiaries should contact the Horticulture Officer of concerned district to avail benefits and assistance under the scheme. Operational Guidelines, cost norms of different interventions being promoted under the mission, contact details of Mission Directors etc. are available on HMNEH web site.
benefits: Benefits include access to subsidies for horticulture development interventions such as planting material, micro-irrigation, protected cultivation, post-harvest management, processing, marketing, beekeeping, horticulture mechanization, training of farmers, nurseries, rejuvenation, area coverage, water resources, market infrastructures, and cold chain infrastructure. Financial assistance is provided based on cost norms for various interventions, with technical and administrative support from State Horticulture Missions (SHM).
financial_support: Under MIDH, Government of India (GOI) contributes 100% of total outlay for developmental programmes in the North Eastern States and Himalayan States. Financial assistance is provided as subsidies based on approved cost norms for various horticulture interventions, released through State Horticulture Missions (SHM) to eligible farmers and beneficiaries.
application_process: 1. Farmers / beneficiaries should contact the Horticulture Officer of the concerned district. 2. Submit necessary data via online forms at the Hortnet Portal. 3. Data is verified at the Block Level to ensure it fits the criteria for the programs. 4. The District Horticulture Officer makes a decision regarding approval of the block horticulture project. 5. The project is forwarded to the state-level agricultural or horticultural department. 6. If the project meets the necessary criteria, it may receive approval at the ministry level.
implementing_agency: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
caveats: Benefits are subject to verification of farmer data at Block Level to ensure eligibility for specific programs
Approval is required at multiple levels: Block, District, State, and Ministry
Only projects meeting necessary criteria receive approval at the ministry level
